course.title: AI course: managing documents with AI
course.subtitle: Practical corporate course for applying AI to document management, with exercises on realistic work, reusable materials and clear governance criteria.
course.summary: Practical corporate course for applying AI to document management, with exercises on realistic work, reusable materials and clear governance criteria.
course.mode: In-person or online lab, with guided exercises and materials adapted to the client.
course.profileDescription: For company teams, operational functions and managers; no programming required.
course.problem: Companies often approach document management through scattered experiments: a few prompts, a few enthusiastic users, many doubts about data, quality and responsibility. This course turns that uncertainty into an operating method. Participants work on realistic scenarios, learn where AI helps, where human review remains essential and how to make the practice repeatable inside the company.
course.audience: For company teams, operational functions and managers; no programming required.
course.whenToChoose: Choose this course when the company wants concrete progress on document management and needs training that produces usable workflows, not abstract theory.
course.chooseIf: When the company wants concrete progress on document management and needs training that produces usable workflows, not abstract theory.
outcomes: Map the work and the decisions where AI can reduce friction.

Define next steps for adoption and governance.

exercises: Map a realistic process connected to document management.

course.privacy: The course uses synthetic, public, anonymised or client-approved materials. It explains how to minimise data exposure, protect confidential information, verify outputs and keep human responsibility explicit.
course.prerequisites: No programming required. Familiarity with the business process is useful.

faqs.question: Is the course tool-specific?
faqs.answer: No. Patterns and workflows are adapted to the tools and policies chosen with the client.

faqs.question: Can company data be used?
faqs.answer: Only when accounts, contracts and internal policies allow it. Otherwise synthetic or anonymised data is used.

faqs.question: What remains after the course?
faqs.answer: Reusable materials, examples, checklists and a clear set of next steps.

faqs.question: Is it theoretical?
faqs.answer: No. The course is built around practical exercises and decisions close to real work.

extraExamples.title: From generic training to the real process
extraExamples.description: A company asks for training on document management, but the real issue emerges during mapping: repeated tasks, informal checks and distributed responsibilities. The path uses examples close to daily work and turns training into an initial operating model, not a theory session.

extraExamples.title: From individual experimentation to governed practice
extraExamples.description: Some people have already found shortcuts with AI while others are blocked. The course creates a shared base: what can be done, what must be reviewed, which data should not be exposed and when escalation is needed. The result is Operating canvas for document management.

extraExamples.title: From enthusiasm to decision
extraExamples.description: Management needs to understand whether document management deserves budget and continuity. The lab separates immediate benefits, operational risks and data dependencies. The company leaves with criteria for the next step instead of more isolated demos.

selectionCriteria: Choose this course if the main need concerns document management, not a generic overview of AI.
Prefer it when there is a process, document, workflow or responsibility to work on during training.
Postpone it if there is no internal sponsor yet or if the issue is only buying a software licence.
Pair it with AI Workflow Redesign Lab when the company first needs to understand which processes deserve priority.
limits: It does not promise full automation or replacement of human responsibility.
It does not require confidential data to be uploaded into unapproved environments.
It is not legal, tax, HR or specialist technical advice when those responsibilities remain with competent functions.
It produces skills, criteria and reusable materials; continued adoption requires sponsorship, governance and internal practice.
